title: Tanzanian Zanzibar Coffee
community: Zanzibar Stone Town — the spiced coffee tradition
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Zanzibar Kahawa — finely ground dark coffee brewed with ginger, cardamom, and cloves in a small pot, served in tiny cups without milk. The ancient Swahili coffee ceremony — more cardamom than coffee, more ritual than beverage.
longDesc: Zanzibar spiced coffee is one of the oldest traditions of the Swahili coast — the coffee served from brass pots by vendors in Stone Town since the Arab era. The spices are as important as the coffee; many Zanzibaris consider it primarily a spice beverage that uses coffee as its medium.
ingredients: 4 tbsp finely ground dark roast coffee
equipment: Small pot or jebena (Ethiopian coffee pot)
steps: Combine water, coffee, cardamom, ginger, and cloves in a small pot.
Remove from heat. Rest 2 minutes for grounds to settle.
Pour slowly into tiny cups, leaving grounds in the pot.
chefTips: Pour slowly — don't disturb the settled grounds.
The coffee should be intense but the spices should be equally present.
cookingScience: The spices in Zanzibar kahawa — particularly cardamom — have volatile aromatic compounds that are released during the brewing boil. Unlike extraction-based brewing, boiling the spices directly extracts both water-soluble and slightly fat-soluble aromatics, producing a more integrated flavour.
sustainabilityTips: Tanzanian coffee — one of the world's finest — from local highland farmers.
culturalNote: Zanzibar spiced coffee is the island's most ancient social ritual — served from brass pots in tiny cups at every gathering, offered to every guest, sipped slowly while the conversation turns. It has been the coffee of Zanzibar's merchants, scholars, and fishermen for centuries.
